description:
Hello everyone! I’m the team lead for the NASA Space Challenge. I’m passionate about space exploration and STEM innovation. I’m familiar with the competition rules, good at project planning, report polishing and team coordination.

We are looking for teammates with any of these skills: research & report writing, graphic design, 3D modeling, creative thinking, or strong execution. No prior competition experience is required. If you are curious about space and ready to collaborate, come join us!
summary: For decades, NASA’s historic missions to the Moon and Mars have left behind a trail of remarkable engineering marvels—from abandoned descent stages and rovers to scientific instruments. To address the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge, we developed an immersive digital storytelling platform that transforms these discarded hardware pieces into narrative-driven historical anchors. By combining archival data, 3D visualizations, and compelling spatial narratives, our project allows users to virtually "visit" these sites and uncover the human stories, scientific triumphs, and environmental reflections behind every piece of space debris. This is important because these celestial relics are not merely trash; they are the fragile archaeological heritage of humanity's first steps into the cosmos, deserving to be preserved, remembered, and understood before time erases them.
details:
1. Overview & How It Works Echoes of the Cosmos: Stories of NASA’s Lunar and Martian Relics is an interactive digital storytelling platform designed to bring NASA’s discarded hardware on the Moon and Mars back into the public consciousness. Users navigate a dual-planet spatial interface—spanning Tranquility Base on the Moon to Jezero Crater on Mars—to inspect abandoned descent stages, rovers, and scientific instruments. By clicking on each artifact, users unlock a multi-layered narrative combining real orbital imagery, 3D hardware models, historical mission timelines, and first-person "hardware logs" that translate raw engineering telemetry into deeply human stories.

2. Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Reframing "Space Junk" as Off-World Heritage: Instead of viewing discarded equipment merely as debris, our platform educates the public on their value as humanity's first extraterrestrial archaeological sites.
  • Accessible Space Education: By turning complex NASA archival data into engaging, bite-sized visual narratives, we lower the barrier for students, educators, and space enthusiasts to connect with planetary exploration history.
  • Advocating for Lunar & Martian Preservation: As humanity prepares for sustained lunar presence under the Artemis program, our project sparks crucial conversations about protecting historic landing sites from future disturbances.

3. Creativity & Unique Approach Rather than presenting a dry encyclopedia or static list of coordinates, we approached space hardware through empathetic storytelling. Each piece of equipment is given a distinct "voice" and narrative arc—from the quiet endurance of the Apollo Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflectors still operating decades later, to the poignant final transmissions of Mars rovers like Opportunity. Blending hard scientific visualization with emotional narrative design creates an unforgettable museum-like experience in the browser.

4. Tools, Tech Stack & NASA Data

  • NASA Open Data: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) imagery, Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) HiRISE data, NASA Planetary Data System (PDS), and NASA 3D Resources.
  • Development & Design Tools: Figma、Canva、Premiere、React

5. Key Factors Considered by Our Team

  • Scientific Accuracy vs. Narrative Engagement: We carefully balanced verified NASA mission parameters, landing coordinates, and hardware specs with accessible, emotionally resonant storytelling.
  • Dual-Planet Contrast: We designed the user experience to highlight the distinct environmental realities of the Moon (airless, static preservation) versus Mars (dust storms, dynamic weathering) and how those environments shape the fate of abandoned equipment.
  • Accessibility & Performance: We optimized visual assets and streamlined the interface so users can smoothly explore the stories across both desktop and mobile devices without heavy hardware requirements.
